info.description:
## Overview

Drishti API is a REST and WebSocket API for Indian market data and derived workflows: news, block deals, symbol metadata, corporate announcements, earnings filings, conference calls, alerts, and AI portfolio summaries.

All routes are versioned under **`/v1`**. Authenticate every request with your API key (`X-API-Key` header or `api_key` query parameter). WebSocket connections use the same key on `wss://developers.manasija.in/v1/ws`.

## Try it quickly

Request examples in this reference are prefilled with sample symbols and parameters. Replace the API key, then execute from the docs UI or your HTTP client.

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `GET /symbols/metadata?symbols=RELIANCE,TCS` | Company metadata for up to 20 symbols |
| `GET /announcements/categories` | Announcement category list |
| `GET /announcements?symbols=RELIANCE&limit=5` | Paginated announcements |
| `GET /earnings?symbols=RELIANCE&limit=3` | Earnings filings |
| `GET /concalls?symbols=RELIANCE&limit=2` | Conference calls |
| `GET /concalls/upcoming?limit=20` | Upcoming conference calls |
| `GET /alerts?symbols=RELIANCE&limit=5` | Market alerts |
| `GET /news?symbols=RELIANCE&limit=5` | News feed |
| `GET /block-deals?symbols=RELIANCE&limit=5` | Structured block-deal prints |

## API access scopes

If your key restricts `apis`, requests outside the allowed products return `403`.

| Scope | Routes (under `/v1`) |
|-------|----------------------|
| `announcements` | `/announcements` |
| `symbols` | `/symbols` |
| `earnings` | `/earnings` |
| `news` | `/news` |
| `block-deals` | `/block-deals` |
| `alerts` | `/alerts` |
| `concalls` | `/concalls` |
| `daily-summary` | `/daily-summary` |
| `batch-summary` | `/batch` |

WebSocket products are authorized separately (per-product addon on your account and optional `ws_channels` restriction on the key).

## Credit billing (REST)

Credits debit only after a successful billable response. Cost is **`credit_cost × units`**, where `units` depends on the route. For block deals, symbol metadata, announcements, earnings, and conference-call lists, `units` equals the number of returned items. For alerts and news, `units` is page-based. Attachment and transcript routes charge per ready item returned. Routes that support `detailed=true` on list endpoints use a higher per-unit rate when `detailed=true` (see product catalog `credit_cost_detailed`).

| Product | Route | Summary rate | With `detailed=true` (list only) |
|---------|-------|--------------|----------------------------------|
| Announcements | `GET /announcements` | 1 credit / returned item | 2 credits / returned item |
| Earnings | `GET /earnings` | 1 credit / returned item | 2 credits / returned item |
| Conference calls | `GET /concalls` | 1 credit / returned item | 2 credits / returned item |
| Upcoming concalls | `GET /concalls/upcoming` | Free | 5 credits / page with results |
| Alerts | `GET /alerts` | 5 credits / page with results | — |
| News | `GET /news` | 1 credit / page with results | — |
| Block deals | `GET /block-deals` | 1 credit / returned item | — |
| Symbols | `GET /symbols/metadata` | 1 credit / returned item | — |
| Daily summary | `POST /daily-summary` | 5 credits / generated summary; no-news/no-signal is free | — |
| Batch summary (submit) | `POST /batch/jobs` | 50 credits / accepted job | — |
| Batch summary (processing) | async per JSONL line | 5 credits / successfully processed item | — |

Attachment routes bill **1 credit per ready item** returned. Transcript routes bill **4 credits per ready item** returned. Batch list, status, cancel, and results routes are free. Category and account inspection routes are free. WebSocket connect/subscribe/delivery does **not** spend credits.

REST **requests/min** and **requests/day** are enforced as one plan-wide bucket per account (from `subscription_plans` / account metadata), not per product. An API key may set lower `rpm` / `daily` caps than the plan.

## Errors

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `401` | Missing or invalid API key |
| `403` | Product, addon, tier, or full-market entitlement not permitted |
| `404` | Resource not found |
| `429` | Rate or quota limit exceeded |
| `402` | Insufficient API credits (application error envelope) |

## WebSocket

**URL:** `wss://developers.manasija.in/v1/ws`

**Authentication:** same API key as REST (`?api_key=<key>` on the WebSocket URL and/or `X-API-Key` on the upgrade request).

### Connection model

1. Open one WebSocket connection.
2. Send one JSON `subscribe` message **per product** you want to receive.
3. The server replies with a per-product acknowledgment (`status`, `product`, `tier`, `full_feed`, `symbols`, `detailed`).
4. Events arrive as JSON text frames: `{"channel": "<product>", "data": { ... }}`.
5. Sending another `subscribe` for the **same** `product` replaces that product’s subscription on this connection; other products on the socket are unchanged.
6. On disconnect, all subscriptions on that connection are released.

Only `op: "subscribe"` is supported. Any other operation returns `{"error": "Unsupported operation"}`.

### Available products

Each product is subscribed independently. Symbol scope is **not shared** across products—even on a single connection you must send a complete `symbols` array (or an explicit full-feed choice) in **every** subscribe message.

| `product` | Stream |
|-----------|--------|
| `news` | News updates |
| `block-deals` | Structured NSE/BSE block-deal / block-trade prints |
| `announcements` | Corporate announcements |
| `earnings` | Earnings filings |
| `concalls` | Conference calls |
| `alerts` | Market alerts |

The product must be enabled as a WebSocket addon on your account and allowed on your API key.

### Subscribe message

```json
{"op": "subscribe", "product": "announcements", "symbols": ["RELIANCE", "TCS"], "detailed": true}
```

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `op` | Yes | Must be `"subscribe"`. |
| `product` | Yes | One of the products in the table above. |
| `symbols` | Yes | Array of symbol strings. Behavior depends on your tier (see below). Symbols are normalized to uppercase. Empty strings are ignored. |
| `detailed` | No | Boolean. Defaults to `true`. For `announcements`, `earnings`, and `concalls`, `true` delivers the same detailed row shape as REST `detailed=true`; `false` delivers the same summary row shape as REST `detailed=false`. `news`, `block-deals`, and `alerts` ignore this field. |

Malformed JSON returns `{"error": "Invalid JSON"}`. A missing `product` returns `{"error": "Missing product"}`. A non-array `symbols` returns `{"error": "symbols must be an array"}`. A non-boolean `detailed` returns `{"error": "detailed must be a boolean"}`.

### Subscription tiers

Your tier is set per product on the account’s WebSocket addon. It appears in the subscribe acknowledgment as `tier`.

| Tier | `symbols` in subscribe | Delivery |
|------|------------------------|----------|
| `starter_100` | Non-empty list required | Events whose payload matches any subscribed symbol. At most **100** active symbols account-wide. |
| `pro_1000` | Non-empty list required | Same as `starter_100`, with a limit of **1,000** active symbols account-wide. |
| `scale` | `[]` **or** a non-empty list | **`[]`:** full broadcast for that product (`full_feed: true` in the ack). **Non-empty list:** symbol-filtered delivery, same matching rules as capped tiers (`full_feed: false`). |

Capped tiers (`starter_100`, `pro_1000`) reject an empty `symbols` array. `scale` is the only tier that may use `[]` for an unfiltered product feed.

Active-symbol limits are enforced **account-wide** across connections and products. There is no monthly unique-symbol cap in the default deployment; operators may enable one via `WS_MONTHLY_UNIQUE_SYMBOLS_ENABLED` if needed. Connect, subscribe, and delivered events do not debit credits.

**Simultaneous connections** are limited **per account** by subscription plan (configured in `product_catalog.yaml` → `subscription_plans.max_ws_connections`). Sandbox is **0**; paid plans (**starter**, **pro**, **scale**) allow **5** concurrent open WebSocket connections. The same physical socket may subscribe to multiple products; it counts as one connection. Re-subscribing on an already-registered connection does not consume an additional slot.

### Usage patterns

**Single product, symbol-filtered (`starter_100` / `pro_1000`):**

```json
{"op": "subscribe", "product": "announcements", "symbols": ["RELIANCE", "TCS"], "detailed": true}
```

**Single product, full broadcast (`scale`):**

```json
{"op": "subscribe", "product": "news", "symbols": []}
```

**Single product, full-market with symbol filter (`scale`):**

```json
{"op": "subscribe", "product": "news", "symbols": ["RELIANCE", "TCS"]}
```

**Multiple products on one connection** — send a separate subscribe message for each product with that product’s own symbol list (or `[]` for full feed where your tier allows it):

```json
{"op": "subscribe", "product": "announcements", "symbols": ["RELIANCE", "TCS"], "detailed": true}
```

```json
{"op": "subscribe", "product": "earnings", "symbols": ["RELIANCE", "INFY", "TCS"], "detailed": false}
```

```json
{"op": "subscribe", "product": "news", "symbols": []}
```

```json
{"op": "subscribe", "product": "block-deals", "symbols": ["RELIANCE", "TCS", "ICICIBANK"]}
```

**Update symbols for one product** — send a new subscribe for that `product` only; other products on the connection keep their previous scope:

```json
{"op": "subscribe", "product": "announcements", "symbols": ["RELIANCE", "TCS", "INFY"], "detailed": false}
```

### Server responses

**Successful subscribe:**

```json
{"status": "subscribed", "product": "announcements", "tier": "starter_100", "full_feed": false, "symbols": ["RELIANCE", "TCS"], "detailed": true}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `status` | `"subscribed"` when accepted. |
| `product` | Product that was configured. |
| `tier` | Your entitlement tier for that product (`starter_100`, `pro_1000`, `scale`, …). |
| `full_feed` | `true` when the connection receives every event for that product; `false` when delivery is limited to `symbols`. |
| `symbols` | Effective symbol list after normalization (empty when `full_feed` is `true`). |
| `detailed` | Effective payload detail mode for this product subscription. Defaults to `true` when omitted. |

**Stream event:**

```json
{"channel": "announcements", "data": { }}
```

The `data` object is the published payload for that product. Symbol-filtered subscriptions receive an event only when a symbol in the payload intersects that product’s subscribed `symbols` on this connection.

For `announcements`, `earnings`, and `concalls`, the event `data` object follows the same field sets as the corresponding REST rows. With `detailed=true` (the default), stream events include the REST detailed fields such as announcement `long_summary` / `extracted_information`, earnings `earnings_significant` / `management_guidance` / `exceptional_items` / `exceptional_items_significant` / `earnings_table` / `results_pages`, and concall `expanded_analysis` when present. With `detailed=false`, streams omit the detailed-only fields and deliver the REST summary row shape. Each stream message also carries `event` when the producer names it; for `earnings` this is `earnings.ready` for the first result of a company-quarter and `earnings.updated` for later changes (a late results table or a later filing).

For `block-deals`, event `data` uses the same public shape as `GET /v1/block-deals` rows:

```json
{
  "channel": "block-deals",
  "data": {
    "id": "68a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b",
    "symbol": "ICICIBANK",
    "company": "ICICI Bank Limited",
    "exchange": "NSE",
    "trade_value_cr": 328.48,
    "shares": 2302036,
    "price": 1426.9,
    "date": "2026-08-10T09:00:38+00:00"
  }
}
```

Headline / title text from the upstream news source is never included on the `block-deals` stream.

**Authorization or limit error:**

```json
{"error": "WebSocket addon 'announcements' is not enabled for this key", "code": "forbidden"}
```

Invalid or missing API keys close the connection with WebSocket close code **4401**.

Return the account profile for your API key.

Use this as the starting point for account dashboards. The response includes account
status, current credit balance, which REST products and live-stream products are
enabled, and entitlement details for WebSocket subscriptions.

Return recent credit activity for your account.

Each ledger entry records a top-up, usage charge, or manual adjustment with a timestamp
and description. Use this to show billing history, reconcile balance changes, or audit
recent API consumption. The `limit` parameter controls how many of the most recent
entries are returned.

post.description:
Submit a batch job by uploading a file of summary requests.

Each line in the file should include a unique request id and either a legacy portfolio
payload or a watchlist-style symbol payload—the same shapes as the daily-summary endpoint,
repeated many times. `context_window_days` has the same 1-7 inclusive Asia/Kolkata
calendar-day semantics as daily summary.
The job is accepted immediately and returns a `batch_*` id. Processing happens in the
background; poll job status and download results when complete. Ideal for overnight
client reports or bulk portfolio digests.

Billed at **50 credits** when the job is accepted. Each successfully processed JSONL
line bills **5 credits** asynchronously when the worker completes.

value.file: <binary: portfolio.jsonl — see description for line format>

delete.description:
Cancel a batch job that is still pending or in progress.

Use this if a job was submitted by mistake or is no longer needed. Jobs that have
already finished (succeeded, partial, failed, or cancelled) cannot be cancelled.
Lines processed before cancellation stay billed and remain downloadable.

get.description:

get.description:
Download the results file for a finished batch job.

Available once processing has ended—successfully, partially, with failures, or by
cancellation (in which case only the lines processed before cancelling are included). Each
line maps back to the original request id and contains either the generated summary
or an error explanation. The response is a downloadable file suitable for importing
into downstream reporting workflows.

schema.title: Job Id

Generate a personalized daily market summary for your portfolio.

news, corporate events, and market context for those symbols and returns a markdown
digest you can render in email, mobile apps, or research tools. Use
`context_window_days` to include up to seven calendar days of prior context when
investigating a move whose catalyst predates today. Best for end-of-day
portfolio briefings rather than symbol-by-symbol data retrieval.

responses are successful but free.

Use these fields to enrich announcement, earnings, and conference-call views with company name, logo, market cap, sector, industry, ISIN, and related classification data. `GET /symbols/metadata` is limited to 20 symbols or scrip codes per request.
tags.name: Symbols

tags.description: Discover exchange filings and corporate announcements as they are published. Browse by symbol, category, or date; open fuller detail when needed; and fetch attachment download links for the original filing documents.
tags.name: Announcements

tags.description: Browse market and company news in a scrolling feed. Filter by symbol, scrip code, sentiment, or date to build watchlist views, research timelines, or sentiment-aware news panels in your application.
tags.name: News

tags.description: Browse structured NSE/BSE block-trade prints with exchange, trade value, shares, and price. Filter by symbol, exchange, or date. Headline text from the upstream news source is never returned.
tags.name: Block deals

tags.description: Track quarterly and annual results for listed companies. Scan recent filings, pull structured earnings data for a specific quarter, and download the underlying result documents when attachments are available.
tags.name: Earnings

tags.description: Follow post-results conference calls and management commentary. See what is coming up, review completed calls with optional analysis, and access transcript or audio recordings for a given symbol and quarter.
tags.name: Conference calls

tags.description: Monitor time-sensitive market and corporate events in one feed. Alerts cover earnings, high-growth concalls, price moves, 52-week highs/lows, and volume spikes. Filter by symbol, type (`52w_high`, `52w_low`, `earnings`, `high_growth_concalls`, `price_alert`, `rvol_alert`, `volume_alert`), date, or a higher-signal important-only view.
tags.name: Alerts

tags.description: Inspect the account tied to your API key without making a data request. Check balance, enabled products, rate limits, live usage, and recent credit activity for dashboards and billing widgets.
tags.name: Account

tags.description: Generate a single AI-written daily digest for a portfolio of holdings. Submit symbols with optional weights and receive a markdown summary of the news and events most relevant to that portfolio. Billed at **5 credits** only when a generated summary is returned; no-news/no-signal responses are free.
tags.name: Daily summary

tags.description: Run the daily-summary workflow at scale. Upload many portfolio requests in one file, receive a job id right away, poll until processing finishes, then download all generated summaries together. Job submission bills **50 credits** on accept; each successfully processed JSONL line bills **5 credits** when the worker completes. List, status, cancel, and results routes are free.
tags.name: Batch summary

tags.description: Receive live updates instead of polling REST endpoints. Subscribe to news, block deals, announcements, earnings, conference calls, or alerts on a single connection and get events pushed as they are published for the symbols you care about.
tags.name: WebSocket
